dependencyDecision.reason: The current 0.1.5 relay depends on Yjs 14 release-candidate protocol packages and failed live update propagation against Syzygy's pinned stable Yjs 13 client. The exact official 0.1.1 line declares yjs ^13.5.6 and passed the same live harness.

proved: Every collaboration provider declares exact realtime, awareness, durable-local, remote-persistence, and attachment capabilities instead of inferring them from a transport name.

The WebSocket binding rejects public plaintext endpoints, non-WebSocket schemes, embedded credentials, query parameters, fragments, prefilled room paths, weak room IDs, and private-address lookalikes.
Two real stable-Yjs-13 clients exchange document updates and ephemeral awareness through an exact pinned y-websocket-compatible relay.
After the relay process exits, independent client edits made during the partition converge after a fresh relay process starts on the same endpoint.
Disconnect publishes an awareness tombstone and the remaining client removes stale presence.
The WebSocket provider composes the existing local IndexedDB provider and automation registry while advertising that the basic relay has no remote persistence.
notProved: Persisted project-manifest migration, product share/join UI, CSP activation, or a packaged app selecting this provider.
Relay authentication/authorization, durable server persistence, backup/restore, quotas, abuse controls, or TLS deployment.
App-process restart restoration through IndexedDB while the relay is unavailable; the live harness keeps both client documents in memory across relay restart.
Five-client rapid-edit soak, large-document latency, hostile binary-frame fuzzing, cross-platform packet capture, or physical two-install use.
A current online registry vulnerability audit; the offline npm audit cache result is not treated as release evidence.
A shipped updater artifact containing this implementation.
